review_type: Narrow source-only continuation of own completed primary/native review; no fresh vote
current_literal_question: Oracle and Sorcerer are the main players. Explain their complete card-selection and swapping sequence, including which card is faceup or facedown at each step and whether their sharing a Planning phase makes the effects simultaneous.

required_facts: Oracle acts before selecting its card, forcing Sorcerer to play faceup.
Oracle sees that card, then selects and plays its own facedown.
Only after both selections may Sorcerer switch encounter cards, before revealing Oracle's card.
The before/after-selection timings govern; not simultaneous merely because both are Planning.
source_references: Printed original Oracle and Sorcerer sheets

current_entry_binding.relationship_to_own12: complete question/key entry identical to own12

decision: Post-exchange location/orientation is supported as straightforward application of exchange; distinguish it from verbatim explicit post-exchange wording. No separate flipping rule supplied.

primary_sources.heading: Alien Interactions

quotes.text: first, forcing the Sorcerer to play his encounter card faceup. The Oracle then looks at that card and selects her encounter card, playing it facedown.
quotes.normalization: Line-break hyphen face-/down joined; extraction line breaks normalized.

quotes.text: If the Sorcerer wishes, he may switch encounter cards with the Oracle before revealing the Oracle’s card.

directly_states: Same phase does not make these powers simultaneous.
Oracle first forces Sorcerer encounter card faceup.
Oracle then selects/plays its own card facedown.
Sorcerer may exchange the selected encounter cards before revealing Oracle original card.

primary_sources.directly_states: Oracle sees opponent card before selecting/playing own card; native power is main-player/mandatory/Planning.

primary_sources.quote: switch encounter cards with your opponent so that he or she reveals your card and you reveal your opponent’s card.
primary_sources.directly_states: Optional exchange after selection/before revelation, with each player revealing the received card; native power is main-player/optional/Planning.

explicit_versus_derived.item: Sorcerer original card is faceup before exchange; Oracle original card is facedown before exchange.
explicit_versus_derived.status: explicit in original rulebook p14 example

explicit_versus_derived.item: If Sorcerer uses Magic, the encounter cards switch sides, and each player reveals the other original card.
explicit_versus_derived.status: explicit exchange/reveal instruction; physical side change is the direct meaning of switch

explicit_versus_derived.item: Immediately after exchange, Sorcerer originally selected faceup card is in front of Oracle, faceup.
explicit_versus_derived.status: straightforward derived physical application; not separately stated word-for-word as a new orientation rule
explicit_versus_derived.rationale: The card was already faceup and is exchanged; neither text instructs turning it facedown.

explicit_versus_derived.item: Oracle originally selected facedown card is now in front of Sorcerer, facedown until Sorcerer reveals it.
explicit_versus_derived.status: derived post-exchange position/orientation, additionally anchored by explicit before revealing Oracle card wording
explicit_versus_derived.rationale: Example supplies facedown Oracle card followed by optional exchange before that card is revealed; native Sorcerer says Sorcerer reveals opponent original card.

explicit_versus_derived.item: Turn the already-faceup card facedown or automatically expose Oracle facedown card as part of exchanging.
explicit_versus_derived.rationale: No allowed passage or either native power inspected prescribes such a step.

minimal_source_backed_wording: If Sorcerer swaps, the originally Sorcerer-selected card moves to Oracle faceup; the originally Oracle-selected card moves to Sorcerer facedown, and Sorcerer later reveals it. This describes applying the stated exchange to the face states established by the example.

orientation_state_trace.step: After Oracle forces Sorcerer to play
After optional Sorcerer exchange, before revealing received card

ownership_language_limit: Originally selected identifies each card origin; current card in front of a player identifies its played encounter role after exchange. Do not infer permanent card ownership or a new rule about eventual hand/discard destinations.
literal_scope_assessment: Q144 already asks complete sequence and face state at each step. This may clarify that existing requested sequence; it is not a new coverage question/group or a new special flipping mechanic.
assumptions_and_limits: Scenario uses the stated native powers and the example optional exchange; no other card effect changes orientation.
Preserving the established face state while physically exchanging is identified as derived application, not a quotation prescribing a separate no-flip rule.
No missing flare/card text, new play permission, permanent ownership or subsequent retention priority invented.
General power reveal ambiguity and other pending human choices are unaffected.
